admission.label: BOUND, not an expected cost: every call of every cell still to run at the input cap, beside everything committed, under the aggregate limit

assumptions.label: ASSUMPTIONS of the bounds, fixed in code and pricing.json: each call's ceiling is its counted input with the margin at the dearest input rate, plus every output token, times the US multiplier; prices as recorded, not a billing guarantee

estimates.label: ESTIMATE, not a bound: the mean calculated cost of earlier cells priced from their usage, on development cases with few observations; not an invoice and not a prediction for the cases planned

fixed5.basis: Phase 2's requests (the historical ledger, ADR-025's fixed top 5) and fixed5 cells of the active ledger

fixed10.basis: no observation: the fixed5 estimate plus 1280 input tokens (five more passages at the 256-token passage budget) at 4 USD per million

agent.basis: agent cells of the active ledger (D1 is one)

notes: An answer is accepted when it matches the answer schema and cites only passages supplied to the model; that is a deterministic check, not evidence that its claims are correct or supported, which needs human review against the cited passages.
Costs are calculated from reported usage and pricing.json, or kept at the reservation where nothing could be priced; they are not an invoice.

The conditions differ by design: A and B send the Phase 2 request with its own system prompt and no tool, once; C appends the search instruction to that system prompt, offers its one search tool and may make three calls, sharing one per-cell time budget across them and its searches. Model, settings, question, editions, initial ranking and answer checks are shared.
Admission figures are bounds (every call at the input cap), not expected costs; estimates come from earlier usage settlements of development cases.
